item.title: Vance America 250: The Complete History of America (Abridged) - A Musical at McGregor Hall — Sat Aug 29, 7:30 PM — McGregor Hall Performing Arts Center
item.description:
The Complete History of America (Abridged) Saturday, August 29, 2026 | 7:30 PM McGregor Hall Performing Arts Center | Henderson, NC
What better way to celebrate the 250th birthday of our country than to enjoy a lighthearted review of the history of these United States! 600 years of history in 6,000 seconds! From Washington to Watergate, yea verily from the Bering Straits to Baghdad, from New World to New World Order – The Complete History of America (Abridged) is a 90-minute rollercoaster ride through the glorious quagmire that is American History, reminding us that it’s not the length of your history that matters — it’s what you’ve done with it! You don’t want to miss this hysterically funny show!
Performances: Friday, August 28 - 7:30 PM Saturday, August 29 - 7:30 PM Sunday, August 30 - 3:00PM
For tickets and information, visit mcgregorhall.org.
Presented by McGregor Hall in partnership with Vance County America 250.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Spy Training 101: Decode a Secret Message — Sun Aug 30 — North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
item.description:
Pretend you’ve been recruited as a member of the Culper Spy Ring, and you need to know how to decipher a message written in invisible ink. Supplies include a paint brush, water, drying cloth, vitriol (diluted sulfuric acid), Thomas Jefferson cipher and “furnace box.” Read the clues to find the coin with a hidden message, reveal the message using the brush and vitriol, then use the cipher to decode the message.
Contact: Nancy Locquet Absillis, nancy.locquet@naturalsciences.org
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Elk Knob State Park: Curious Minds Adventure Scavenger Hunt — Sun Aug 30, 7:00 AM — Elk Knob State Park
item.description:
Join the Curious Minds Adventure Scavenger Hunt at Elk Knob State Park. Journey through northern hardwood forest, follow winding mountain trails, and explore the unique ecosystems of this high-elevation park. Keep your eyes open—what signs of wildlife or weather-shaped landscapes will you uncover? Look for unique rocks that make Elk Knob a very special clue in North Carolina’s geologic history. Start at the Visitor Center and scan the QR code in your Actionbound app. Flyers with the QR code will be placed in the Park Office and on all park map kiosks.
The adventures are available on the Actionbound app – a free download to your cellphone through your phone’s app store. There’s no need to create a profile and no personal data is collected with Actionbound. You simply find new hunts by searching for the park name or scanning the associated QR code posted for your park’s adventure.
This program is made possible through a partnership with the NC Science Trail (ncsciencetrail.org)! Visit

item.title: America 250 Locomotive Celebration — Sun Aug 30, 8:00 AM — North Carolina Transportation Museum
item.description:
The N.C. Transportation Museum, Trains Magazine, and White River Productions are excited to announce the America 250 Locomotive Celebration August 28-30 at the N.C. Transportation Museum in Spencer, NC!
Experience a once-in-a-generation railroading event as the N.C. Transportation Museum hosts the first and only gathering of commemorative locomotives from Class I, short line, and passenger railroads, all specially painted to celebrate America’s semiquincentennial.
Set against the iconic Bob Julian Roundhouse, this extraordinary display of red, white, and blue locomotives is expected to create one of the most memorable railroad photography opportunities of the America 250 celebration.

item.title: Mecklenburg's Declaration: NC's Revolutionary Presbyterians — Tue Sep 1 — Presbyterian Heritage Center
item.description:
An article published in the April 30, 1819 edition of the Raleigh Register and North Carolina Gazette proclaimed the following: “It is not probably known to many of our readers, that the citizens of Mecklenburg County, in this State, made a Declaration of Independence more than a year before Congress made theirs. The following Document on the subject has lately come to the hands of the Editor from unquestionable authority, and is published that it may go down to posterity.”
The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.
But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting.

item.title: Native Plant Gardens Volunteer Day - NC the Beautiful — Tue Sep 1, 9:00 AM — Gorges State Park - Grassy Ridge Access & Visitor Center
item.description:
Located at the Park’s Visitor Center, the newly established Native Landscape Garden's mission is to teach visitors to the park about native plants and their importance as well as the native pollinator species that rely on them. On the first Tuesday of each month, beginning July 7 and continuing through November 3, join Park Rangers to perform maintenance on the gardens so they continue to serve as a living native plant education opportunity to all who view them. Bring work gloves, water, hats and weather-appropriate clothing. Volunteers will receive a Friends of Gorges State Park Volunteer T-Shirt. For more information or to sign up, go to https://www.signupgenius.com/go/10C0B4CAAAC28A5FAC25-64387146-native
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Choosing Sides: The Catawba Nation & The Fight for Independence — Tue Sep 1, 10:00 AM — Kings Mountain Historical Museum
item.description:
In partnership with the Catawba Cultural Center, Kings Mountain Historical Museum is excited to present, "Choosing Sides: The Catawba Nation & the Fight for Independence." This exhibit explores the critical role of the Catawba Nation, also known as Yį Iswąre or “People of the River,” in the American Revolutionary War, particularly in the backcountry regions of Tryon and Lincoln Counties. As skilled warriors, guides, and allies of the Patriot cause, the Catawba people defended their homeland, protected settler communities, and contributed to pivotal battles. Despite the hardships of disease, displacement, and warfare, the Catawba demonstrated extraordinary resilience. Their story is one of courage, alliance, and survival, woven into the struggle for independence in the Southern Campaign of the Revolution.
The exhibit will run from June 30, 2026 until October 24, 2026. Admission is Free!
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage — Tue Sep 1, 10:00 AM — Gregg Museum of Art & Design
item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: The Akwari Symposium: "The Science of Bite-sized Well-being During Uncertain Times: Evidence, Practice and Resources to Share" — Wed Sep 2, 7:00 AM — Trent Semans Center for Health Education - Great Hall
item.description:
Title of Presentation: "The Science of Bite-sized Well-being During Uncertain Times: Evidence, Practice and Resources to Share"
Speaker: J. Bryan Sexton, PhD Chief Wellness Officer Director, Duke Center for the Advancement of Well-being Science Duke Health Integrated Practice
The Akwari Society Symposium at Duke University is an annual event hosted by the Duke Department of Surgery. It honors Dr. Onyekwere E. Akwari, the first African-American surgeon on Duke's faculty and centers on holistic excellence in surgery, humanism in patient care, and mentorship.
Mission: To honor and propagate humanism in the practice of surgery
Vision: Human Values as Core Surgical Values
Values: Compassion, Empathy, Integrity, Excellence, Professionalism, Humility, Respect, Service

item.title: Mecklenburg's Declaration: NC's Revolutionary Presbyterians — Thu Sep 3 — Presbyterian Heritage Center
item.description:
An article published in the April 30, 1819 edition of the Raleigh Register and North Carolina Gazette proclaimed the following: “It is not probably known to many of our readers, that the citizens of Mecklenburg County, in this State, made a Declaration of Independence more than a year before Congress made theirs. The following Document on the subject has lately come to the hands of the Editor from unquestionable authority, and is published that it may go down to posterity.”
The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.
But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting.

item.description:

item.title: Choosing Sides: The Catawba Nation & The Fight for Independence — Thu Sep 3, 10:00 AM — Kings Mountain Historical Museum
item.description:
In partnership with the Catawba Cultural Center, Kings Mountain Historical Museum is excited to present, "Choosing Sides: The Catawba Nation & the Fight for Independence." This exhibit explores the critical role of the Catawba Nation, also known as Yį Iswąre or “People of the River,” in the American Revolutionary War, particularly in the backcountry regions of Tryon and Lincoln Counties. As skilled warriors, guides, and allies of the Patriot cause, the Catawba people defended their homeland, protected settler communities, and contributed to pivotal battles. Despite the hardships of disease, displacement, and warfare, the Catawba demonstrated extraordinary resilience. Their story is one of courage, alliance, and survival, woven into the struggle for independence in the Southern Campaign of the Revolution.
The exhibit will run from June 30, 2026 until October 24, 2026. Admission is Free!
Source: NC Cultural Resources

Join us at Fort Fisher State Historic Site on September 5, 2026 for a special pop-up event about our favorite furry friends!
Discover the stories of the pets, mascots, and other animals that left their mark on the Civil War. Learn how these faithful companions provided comfort, companionship, and a sense of humanity to soldiers, and hear about the animals that belonged to individual soldiers, entire companies, and those that called Fort Fisher home.
Stop by to dive deeper, and explore how community partners in and around Wilmington provide care for animals today! Learn from special displays about how humans and animals interact at home and in the wild. You might even meet a furry friend looking for a forever home!
Leashed pets are welcome and encouraged outdoors and on the walking trails. Please note that only service animals are permitted to enter the Visitor Center.
Please consider carpooling with friends and family wherever possible! Limited extra parking is available at Battle

item.title: The Lake's Last Weekend — Sat Sep 5, 10:00 AM — Hanging Rock State Park
item.description:
Labor Day Weekend will be the last time the lake is open for swimming and boating for the year. For additional information reach out to hanging.rock@ncparks.gov

item.title: Ft. Macon Cannon Day — Sat Sep 5, 10:30 AM — Fort Macon State Park
item.description:
Come down to Fort Macon and learn how the different cannons of the fort were loaded, aimed, and shot.
Cannon firing demonstrations will be held at 10:30 a.m.; 11:30 a.m.; 1:30 p.m.; 2:30 p.m.; and 3:30 p.m.
Photo by J. Hill: 10-inch mortar demonstration during Labor Day Weekend Cannon Day at Ft. Macon State Park.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: "Field & Factory: A Look at Tobacco’s Laborers" at Duke Homestead — Sat Sep 5, 11:15 AM — Duke Homestead
item.description:
To learn a fuller story of the people who worked in tobacco, join Duke Homestead staff on site for a special program, “Field & Factory: A Look at Tobacco’s Laborers.” These walks will highlight the contributions that each group of people working in tobacco made to North Carolina’s culture and powerful economy in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, while addressing the inequalities in tobacco’s labor forces.
We will depart from the visitor’s center lobby at 11:15am and 2:15pm on Saturday, September 5th, 12th, 19th, and 26th. Admission is free.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Tour of Ft. Macon 12:00 Noon — Sat Sep 5, 12:00 PM — Fort Macon State Park
item.description:
On Cannon days there will only be one Fort Tour scheduled at 12:00 noon.
Tours last about 45 minutes.
Meet at the fort entrance. Pets are not allowed inside the fort.
Photo by C. Peek: The fort at Fort Macon State Park
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Canoe Hike — Sat Sep 5, 5:00 PM — Carvers Creek State Park - Long Valley Farm Access
item.description:
We will be learning the basics of canoeing and then trying out our new skills by maneuvering through the Cypress swamp. This is a slow and calm canoeing experience and great for beginners or if you want to get a closer look at the Cypress trees. YOU MUST SIGN-UP. You can call the park office to sign-up. Limit is 10 visitors. Please allow approximately 15 minutes to walk from the parking lot to the Rain Shelter. Age requirement- 8 years old and older.
Source: NC Cultural Resources
